subject: Use when designing or reviewing HTTP-based systems where method semantics, status codes, idempotency, safe methods,…

evals.prompt: Define http-semantics in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the http-semantics skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind http-semantics. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.
A user asks: "design the JSON shape of the request and response bodies (use api-design)". Should http-semantics activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force http-semantics onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to system-interface-contracts, api-design, webhook-integration, route-handler-design, client-server-boundary, semantics, code-review.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "decide whether bulk-update should be PUT or PATCH". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying http-semantics.

Place http-semantics among its adjacent skills (system-interface-contracts, api-design, webhook-integration, route-handler-design, client-server-boundary, semantics, code-review). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about http-semantics and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
